2. CAESAREAN SECTION:

Informed decision about child birth – so offer evidence-based information.

Info during AN period to all women

Risk of C/S 1 – in 4.

Info includes:

Indications

Procedure involved

Risks/ Benefits.

Implications for future pregnancies

& birth after C/S.

Discuss Risk/ Benefits of C/S & NVD.

C/S:

Risk of:

Perineal/ Abdominal Pain 3 days PP

Injury to Vagina

Early PPH

Obs shock

Risk of:

Neonatal ICU Admission

Hospital stay

Hysterectomy due to PPH

Cardiac arrest.

Maternal request for C/S due to anxiety – Mental health support.

No C/S due to obesity.

Factors reducing likelihood of Caesarean Section:

Continuous support.

Partogram with 4 hours’ action line.

Consultant obs involved in decision making for C/S.

No influence of Likelihood of Caesarean Section:

Walking in labour

Non supine in II stage of labour.

Water birth

Epidural analgesia

Use of raspberry leaves.

Don’t offer early amniotomy and active management of labor to reduce risk.

Elective C/S after 39 weeks.

Classification of Caesarean Section

Cat – 3:No compromise but requiring early deliveryCat – 4:EL – LSCS birth timed to build women or healthcare provider

Cat – 1:

- Within 30 min

- Immediate Threat

to mom/ baby

examples:

1. Cord Prolapse.

2. Uterine rupture.

3. Major abruption.

4. fetal bradycardia.

 

Cat – 2:

75 min of decision making

Materal/ fetal compromise

That is not immediate threat to life

Pre – OP Testing/ Prepration:

All women:

CBC.

Antibody screening.

Blood grouping.

4 – 8% risk of blood loss > 1 lit.

Uncomplicated pregnancies:

No need of:

Cross match.

Clotting screening.

USG for placental Localization.

Indwelling Catheter

 

Women in Spinal Anaesthesia:

Prophylactic I/V infusion of phenylephirine immediately after S/A to reduce hypotension. Rate of infusion can be adjusted to keep B.P @ 90% or more.

I/V ephedrine boluses to manage B.P if it is < 90% in case pt is on Phenylephirine infusion.

I/V cystalloid co – loading in addision to vasopressors to reduce risk of hypotension.

Anaesthesia:

Information regarding different types of analgesia

Offer regional Anaesthesia including previa.

Care in OT in PT with regional Anaesthesia – because it don’t Anxiety

Before Anaesthesia

Antacids offer before anaesthesia – C/S.

Antiemetics offer.

General Anaesthesia:

Pre oxygenation.

Cricoid pressure.

Rapid sequence induction to reduce aspiration.

150 tilt of OT table.

Warm I/V fluids and blood products to reduce temperature to 370C in pts with shivering.

Use warm irrigation fluids and products.

Surgical Techniques for C/S:

Double Gloves – HIV pts.

Safe surgical practices to reduce HIV.

Alcohol base chlorhexedine skin preparation before C – Section.

Aqueous povidone – iodine vaginal preparation before C – section in women with PROM to reduce risk of endometriosis.

Incision Joel Cohen (R):

Straight – 3cm from pubic symphesis.

Other skin Incisions:

Midline

Low transverse

Straight

Higher incision in class 3 obesity.

Blunt dissection:

OP time.

Fertile Morbidity.

Blunt uterine incision/ dissection:

When lower segment well formed it reduces Hge, Blood loss and need for transfusion

Laceration of fetus 2%.

Forceps – in difficulty delivering the baby’s head.

Uterotonies 5IU I/V.

CCT – endometriotis.

Exteriorisation of uterus = Not recommended.

I/peritoneal repair = recommended.

Less pain, less Op time.

Uterine closure:

Double layer.

Peritoneal closure NR.

Non Closure:

Operative time.

Need for post op analgesia.

Maternal satisfaction.

Abdominal wall closure.

Midline – mass closure dehescience, hernias.

 

S/Cutaneus Tissue Closure.

If > 2cm

S/C drains NR

U/A PH all C/S due to suspected fetal compromise.

A/B Treatment:

Before skin incision (R).

Post OP A/B That r effective against UTI, Endomertritis and wound infectious => 8% risk after C/S.

Don’t give Amoxiclave before skin incision.

1st line:

Cefuroxime 1.5g I/V stat

+ Metronidazole 500mg I/V stat

before cord clamping.

2nd line:

Clindamycin 600mg I/V + stat

Pre cord clamping.

Extended prophylaxis NR.

Paediatrician should be available @ C/S

If there is fetal compromise or G.A is given.

Thermal care: Recommended

Skin to skin contact: Recommended

B.F recommended as soon as possible.

Care after C/S:

HDU need 9/1000 women with C/S.

1 – 1 monitoring until regained airway control and haemodynamic stability and pt is able to communicate.

Monitoring:

HR, RR, B.P, Pain, Sedation, O2 Saturation ½ hourly till satisfactory/ stable.

Intrathecal opioids:

O2 Saturation, RR, Sedation, Pain Score, - 1 hourly till:

Morphine – 24 hours.

Diamorphine – 12 hours.

Epidural Opioids/ PCA:

Hourly throughout treatment (RR, Sedation, Pain score).

2 hours after discontinuation.

Pain Management:

Diamorphine

Intrathecal – 300ug.

Epidural – up to 3ug.

If diamorphine is not available than use:

Intrathecal preservative free morphine (up to 100mg).

Epidermal preservative free morphine (up to 3mg).

NSAIDS if no C/I.

Oral Morphine sulphate – risk of nausea.

I/V PCA using morphine + hourly monitoring of SATS, RR, Sedation.

Paracetamol

Di hydrocodeine.

Co dydramol.

Tramal or oxycodeine at lowest effective dose.

Eating/ Drinking when hungry or thirsty who r well.

Catheter after 12 hours of spinal or top up dose of epidural.

Resp Physiotherapy: NR.

Hospital stay:

NVD 1 – 2 D.

C/S 3 – 4 D.

Discharge after 24 hours if well.

Regular analgesia.

 

Wound Care:

Remove dressing after 6 – 24 hours.

Fever monitoring.

Assessment regarding signs of infection.

Loose clothing

Washing and drying daily.

Negative pressure dressing if BMI > 35 Kg/m2.

Post OP urinary symptoms:

Due to:

UTI 1%.

SUI 4%.

Injuries of Urinar Tract 1/1000 C/S.

Urinary retention.

Post Op Bleeding

Heavy/ irregular due to endometritis less likely RPOCs.

Resumption of Activities (physical, sexual, exercise)

once recovered from C/S.
